                                                            Abstract
     We study unconstrained Online Linear Optimization with Lipschitz losses. The goal is to simultane-
     ously achieve (i) second order gradient adaptivity; and (ii) comparator norm adaptivity also known
     as “parameter freeness” in the literature. Existing regret bounds (Cutkosky and Orabona,√      2018;
     Mhammedi and Koolen, 2020; Jacobsen and Cutkosky, 2022) have the suboptimal O( VT log VT )
     dependence
        √         on the gradient variance VT , while the present work improves it to the optimal rate
     O( VT ) using a novel continuous-time-inspired algorithm, without any impractical doubling trick.
     This result can be extended to the setting with unknown Lipschitz constant, eliminating the range
     ratio problem from prior works (Mhammedi and Koolen, 2020).
          Concretely, we first show that the aimed simultaneous adaptivity can be achieved fairly easily
     in a continuous time analogue of the problem, where the environment is modeled by an arbitrary
     continuous semimartingale. Then, our key innovation is a new discretization argument that pre-
     serves such adaptivity in the discrete time adversarial setting. This refines a non-gradient-adaptive
     discretization argument from (Harvey et al., 2023), both algorithmically and analytically, which
     could be of independent interest.1

     The most natural idea is to apply the CT algorithm to DT as is, and characterize the performance

approach requires a terminal condition at a fixed time horizon T , which is missing from many
common settings of adaptive online learning. Harvey et al. (2023) proposed a particularly strong
and elegant alternative: replacing the standard derivative ϕ′t (St ) in the CT algorithm by the discrete

3. Warm up: Adaptivity in continuous time

problem, in order to demonstrate the inherent simplicity of simultaneous adaptivity. The restriction
